etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowed from Middle French subterfuge m, from Medieval Latin subterfugium n, from Latin subterfugiō (“to flee secretly”), from subter (“under”) and fugiō (“to flee”).
senses: (countable) An indirect or deceptive device or stratagem; a blind. Refers especially to war and diplomatics.
(uncountable) Deception; misrepresentation of the true nature of an activity.
